subject: History
description: Tipu Sultan, the 'Tiger of Mysore' — life, Anglo-Mysore wars, military innovations (rocket warfare), administration, death at Srirangapatna 1799.

questions.stem: TIPU SULTAN, the 'Tiger of Mysore', was killed in which battle?
questions.explanation: TIPU SULTAN was killed on 4 MAY 1799 during the FOURTH ANGLO-MYSORE WAR at the SIEGE OF SERINGAPATAM (SRIRANGAPATNA), his capital. British forces under LORD CORNWALLIS's earlier setup, completed by GENERAL HARRIS, broke through the fort walls; Tipu fought hand-to-hand and was killed. He was 48. KEY BATTLES — ANGLO-MYSORE WARS: (1) FIRST (1767-69) — Hyder Ali (Tipu's father) FORCED British to TREATY OF MADRAS. (2) SECOND (1780-84) — Hyder Ali died (1782); Tipu continued; ended with TREATY OF MANGALORE — generally favourable to Mysore. (3) THIRD (1789-92) — vs Cornwallis; ended with TREATY OF SERINGAPATAM — Tipu lost half his territory + paid 3 crore indemnity + sent 2 sons as hostages. (4) FOURTH (1799) — vs Wellesley; Tipu killed; Mysore split among allies. AFTERMATH: WODEYAR DYNASTY restored to throne under British paramountcy. TIPU's SWORD + WAR ROCKETS captured by British, displayed in London/Edinburgh; some recovered post-2000 by Indian collectors. TIPU'S TIGER (toy organ depicting tiger mauling British soldier) is in the Victoria & Albert Museum, London. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'death of Tipu' is a top SSC, UPSC, MPSC fact — 1× per cycle.

questions.explanation: SRIRANGAPATNA (or SERINGAPATAM, Anglicized) — Tipu Sultan's capital, on an ISLAND in the KAVERI river, ~15 km north of present-day MYSURU (Mysore). KEY FEATURES: massive FORT, RANGANATHASWAMY temple, MASJID-E-ALA (mosque), DARIA DAULAT BAGH (summer palace), GUMBAZ (mausoleum of Hyder Ali, Tipu, and Tipu's mother). BACKGROUND: Sri Ranganathaswamy temple is one of the PANCHA-RANGAS (5 sacred Vishnu temples on Kaveri) — Adi Ranga at Srirangapatna; Madhya Ranga at Shivanasamudra; Antya Ranga at Srirangam (Tamil Nadu). HYDER ALI (Tipu's father) — ascended to power as commander of Wodeyar Mysore army; effectively took over Mysore in 1761. Tipu took over fully in 1782 after Hyder's death. CAPITAL CHOICE: Srirangapatna is naturally fortified by river; strategic location to control southern Karnataka and access to Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra. TODAY: a town of ~25,000; UNESCO Tentative World Heritage List (since 2014, jointly with Hyder Ali sites). VISIT: Daria Daulat Bagh is famous for murals depicting battles, including Tipu's victory over British forces. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'capital of Tipu' is a 1× per cycle SSC, UPSC, MPSC fact.

questions.stem: Tipu Sultan is credited as a PIONEER of which military innovation?
questions.explanation: TIPU SULTAN — pioneered the WORLD's first IRON-CASED WAR ROCKETS (Mysorean rockets). DESIGN: iron tubes (vs. earlier bamboo/cardboard); range up to 1.5-2 km; effective against cavalry and dense formations. MASS PRODUCTION: ~5,000 rocketeers in Tipu's army. KEY USE: BATTLE OF POLLILUR (1780) — Mysorean rockets devastated British East India Company forces, contributing to the British defeat. The rockets struck a British ammunition cart, causing a catastrophic explosion. INTERNATIONAL IMPACT: after Tipu's defeat (1799), captured rockets were sent to BRITAIN's Royal Arsenal in Woolwich. Sir WILLIAM CONGREVE studied them, leading to the 'Congreve rockets' — used in Napoleonic Wars and the War of 1812 (Bombardment of Fort McHenry, 1814 — inspiring 'rockets' red glare' in the US national anthem!). RECENT: Indian space scientist VIKRAM SARABHAI cited Mysorean rockets as inspiration; APJ Abdul Kalam noted them in his autobiography 'Wings of Fire'. ROCKET PARK at Pataluru (Tamil Nadu) — commemorates Tipu's rocket warfare. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'Tipu's rocket innovation' is a top UPSC, SSC, MPSC fact — 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests military-technology history.

questions.stem: Tipu Sultan's father, who founded Mysore's military power, was:
questions.explanation: HYDER ALI (1722-1782) — Tipu Sultan's father. Born in BUDIKOTE (near Kolar, Karnataka) to a humble military family. Joined the WODEYAR Mysore army; rose through ranks via military genius. By 1761, he was de-facto ruler of Mysore (the Wodeyar king Krishnaraja Wodeyar II was reduced to figurehead). EXPANSION: Hyder conquered Bednur, Sondh, Sera, parts of Malabar, Coorg. CONFLICT WITH BRITISH: First Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69) — Hyder forced the British to seek peace; SECOND ANGLO-MYSORE WAR (1780-84) — fought brilliantly; allied with Marathas, Nizam, French; British struggled. Hyder died of cancer in 1782 mid-war; Tipu took over. KEY MILITARY INNOVATIONS: (1) Modernized army with FRENCH advisors. (2) Used cavalry effectively. (3) Pioneered the rocket corps (which Tipu expanded). DIPLOMATIC: maintained correspondence with Ottomans, French, even Napoleon. MODERN VIEW: Hyder is hailed in Karnataka as a regional hero; portraits in state legislative buildings. CONTRASTING NARRATIVE: some communities accuse him of religious persecution during Malabar campaigns (debated by historians). PYQ FREQUENCY: 'Tipu's father' is a 1-mark guaranteed SSC, UPSC, MPSC MCQ.

questions.stem: Tipu Sultan formally ALLIED with which European power against the British?
questions.explanation: TIPU SULTAN cultivated a strong DIPLOMATIC ALLIANCE with FRANCE — the British East India Company's biggest European rival. He sent EMBASSIES to Paris (1788) and corresponded with NAPOLEON BONAPARTE. Tipu wrote Napoleon expressing alliance interest; Napoleon WROTE BACK from Cairo (1798) during his Egyptian campaign — reportedly saying he was looking forward to liberating India from British hands by joining with Tipu. KEY MOVES: (1) Stationed ~300 FRENCH OFFICERS in his army (training, weapons). (2) Planted a 'TREE OF LIBERTY' in his capital after the French Revolution — declared himself 'Citizen Tipu'. (3) Joined the JACOBIN Club of Mysore (a French Revolution inspired political club). BRITISH PARANOIA: French + Tipu alliance was the British strategic NIGHTMARE — fueled the urgency of Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance system. The 4TH ANGLO-MYSORE WAR (1799) was triggered by RICHARD WELLESLEY's anxiety about Tipu's French connections (after Napoleon invaded Egypt 1798). NAPOLEON'S Egyptian campaign was partly aimed at threatening British India; defeated by British naval power (Nelson at Battle of Nile, 1798). PYQ FREQUENCY: Tipu-France alliance is a top UPSC, SSC, MPSC fact — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which Governor-General of British India led the FOURTH ANGLO-MYSORE WAR against Tipu?
questions.explanation: LORD RICHARD WELLESLEY (Governor-General 1798-1805) — initiated the FOURTH ANGLO-MYSORE WAR (1799) against Tipu Sultan. STRATEGIC AIM: eliminate Tipu (a French ally) before Napoleon could reach India. WELLESLEY's KEY INNOVATIONS — SUBSIDIARY ALLIANCE SYSTEM: Indian rulers were forced to accept British 'protection' in exchange for ceding territory and accepting British military stationing. First applied to Hyderabad (1798); after Tipu's fall, expanded to Mysore (Wodeyar restored), Awadh, Marathas, etc. WELLESLEY'S BROTHER — Arthur Wellesley (later DUKE OF WELLINGTON) — was a major commander in the 1799 Mysore campaign and the 2nd Anglo-Maratha War; later defeated Napoleon at WATERLOO (1815). EARLIER GOVERNOR-GENERALS — sequence: (1) Warren Hastings (1773-85) — first under Regulating Act 1773. (2) Lord Cornwallis (1786-93) — won 3rd Anglo-Mysore War; introduced PERMANENT SETTLEMENT in Bengal (1793). (3) Sir John Shore (1793-98). (4) Lord Wellesley (1798-1805). LATER: Lord Cornwallis returned for a brief 2nd term (1805); Lord Minto, Lord Hastings, etc. KEY PYQ ANGLE: Wellesley = 4th Mysore War; Cornwallis = 3rd; Hastings = 1st & 2nd planning. SSC, UPSC, MPSC routinely test this.

questions.stem: Tipu Sultan kept his TIGER throne in which form?

options.option_text: A jeweled throne with tiger motifs
Plain wooden throne with no design
Throne shaped like an elephant only

questions.explanation: TIGER (HUMA) THRONE — Tipu Sultan's GOLDEN-JEWELED OCTAGONAL THRONE, with eight tiger heads supporting it; surmounted by a HUMA bird (mythical Persian bird associated with sovereignty). BUILT: ~1787, ~10 feet wide, weighed many maunds, encrusted with diamonds, rubies, emeralds, pearls. SYMBOLISM: Tipu chose tiger imagery — his personal emblem ('I would rather live one day as a tiger than 100 years as a sheep') — and the 'BUBRI' (tiger-stripe) pattern adorned his court banners, weapons, even uniforms. POST-1799: After Tipu's death, the British looted Srirangapatna for THREE WEEKS (despite Wellesley's orders); the throne was DISMANTLED and parts dispersed. The HUMA bird is in WINDSOR CASTLE (gifted to King George III); other gold tiger heads ended up in the British royal collection, V&A Museum, and private collections. TIPU'S TIGER (toy organ depicting tiger mauling British soldier) — captured at Srirangapatna; now in V&A Museum, London. RECENT: in 2009, Tipu's GOLDEN BIRD (one of the eight) sold at SOTHEBY'S for ~£400,000. INDIA's CULTURAL DIPLOMACY: ongoing efforts to repatriate looted artifacts (like Kohinoor diamond, also from Punjab via Wodeyars in 1799). PYQ FREQUENCY: cultural-history MCQs in UPSC, KAS optional 1× per cycle.
